policies.summary: When the commission issues a certificate, it preempts any local rule that prohibits, regulates or is more restrictive than the certificate, and zoning changes made after the application cannot limit the facility; local ordinances also may not bar site testing.

Developers of solar of 50 MW or more, wind of 100 MW or more, or storage of 50 MW and 200 MWh or more may seek a siting certificate from the Public Service Commission, and a local unit may ask the commission to require one; if the local unit has a compatible renewable energy ordinance the developer must apply locally first, and smaller projects stay under local zoning.

Certificated facilities must meet statutory standards: solar and storage 300 ft from nonparticipating dwellings and 50 ft from property lines and roads, solar panels no taller than 25 ft, wind turbines 2.1 times tip height from nonparticipating residences, 30 hours a year shadow flicker, and 55 dBA at nonparticipating dwellings. A local ordinance stricter than these standards is not "compatible".

restrictions.description: Proactive pause on data center, battery energy storage, and large-scale solar and wind applications pending permanent regulations. Active as of 2026-07-31. Legal basis: Ordinance 2026-07, under the Michigan Zoning Enabling Act (PA 110 of 2006).

Zoning ordinance does not address BESS, solar farms or data centers; PA 233 shift of siting authority; desire to preserve agricultural land. Active as of 2026-09-23; the Township Board adopted the six-month moratorium resolution 5-0 on 2026-04-20, so it runs to about 2026-10-20 unless extended; the Planning Commission was still drafting solar/wind/battery rules during the moratorium period in July 2026. Legal basis: Casco Township Board Resolution to Establish a Moratorium on the Issuance of Zoning Permits for Battery Energy Storage Systems, Solar Energy Farms, and Data Centers (adopted 2026-04-20; resolution number illegible in the posted scan).

Township study of regulations for principal-use solar and wind facilities. Active as of 2026-09-23; Ordinance No. 566 (adopted 2026-03-16) pauses acceptance and processing of applications for principal-use solar and wind facilities for one year, to about 2027-03-16. Legal basis: Charter Township of Comstock (Kalamazoo County) Ordinance No. 566, An Ordinance to Enact a Temporary Moratorium on Principal Use Solar and Wind Renewable Energy Facilities.

Denial of Ranger Power's Heartwood II solar permit and PA 233 concerns; board direction to pause wind, battery and data center projects. Pending as of 2026-09-23; Planning Commission recommended a one-year moratorium in July 2026 with board adoption expected in August; adoption not confirmed. [VERIFY instrument number; adoption date; primary source (news-only evidence) not confirmed at confidence 0.6 in the 2026-09 refresh]. Legal basis: Proposed township resolution/moratorium recommended by the Fayette Township Planning Commission.

Public health, safety, and welfare concerns about battery energy storage systems. Active as of 2026-09-23; Ordinance No. 196 bars new BESS applications through 2026-12-21. Legal basis: Gun Plain Charter Township Ordinance No. 196, temporary moratorium on future BESS applications (preceded by Resolution 2026-9).

Public concerns about impacts of data centers and large renewable energy projects on health, safety, welfare and land uses. Active as of 2026-09-23; one-year moratorium on applications for data centers and large renewable energy projects (solar and storage 50 MW+, wind 100 MW+, hybrids 50 MW+) effective 2026-07-02 runs to 2027-07-02 unless zoning amendments take effect sooner or it is extended. Legal basis: Ordinance No. 2026-06-02, Zoning Ordinance Amendment: Temporary Moratorium Authority, Data Center Temporary Moratorium and Temporary Large Renewable Energy Projects Moratorium (adopted 2026-06-09, effective 2026-07-02), under PA 246 of 1945 and PA 110 of 2006.

No data center use in zoning ordinance; desire to study health, safety and welfare impacts and avoid exclusionary-zoning claims. Pending as of 2026-09-23; moratorium instruments were placed for Board votes on 2026-05-19, 2026-06-16 and 2026-08-18, but adoption outcomes were not found in published materials. [VERIFY adoption date not confirmed at confidence 0.6 in the 2026-09 refresh]. Legal basis: Proposed Resolution 2026-10; proposed Ordinance No. 237 (non-zoning temporary moratorium on data centers and battery energy storage systems); proposed Ordinance No. 238 (zoning ordinance amendment adding Chapter 22 temporary moratorium on data centers).

Planning commission needs time to recommend additional standards for the county solar and battery zoning ordinance (setbacks, acreage cap, host agreement, decommissioning). Extended; active as of 2026-09-23. On 2026-09-22 the Board of Commissioners extended the moratorium a third time, to 2026-12-29, while the solar and battery ordinance amendments go to public hearing. Legal basis: Board of Commissioners resolution imposing a 3-month moratorium on special use permits for Utility Scale Solar Energy Facilities and Battery Energy Storage Systems (May 12, 2026 agenda, Legislative item 2); extension resolutions of 2026-08-11, early September 2026 and 2026-09-22.

Harbor Farmz announced intent to sell its 2839 Full Circle Drive property to a data center developer; concerns about noise, water use, fire risk from lithium-ion batteries and utility strain. Active as of 2026-09-23; resolution moratorium runs through 2027-08-16. The City Commission gave first reading on 2026-09-21 to a zoning ordinance amendment embedding the moratorium; public hearing and second reading are scheduled for 2026-10-05, which staff say would restart a one-year clock. Legal basis: City Commission resolution establishing a moratorium on the acceptance and/or processing of applications for Data Centers, Battery Energy Storage Systems, Cryptocurrency Mining Centers, and AI Data Centers (Aug. 17, 2026 agenda item); companion zoning ordinance amendment pending.

Public concern in other municipalities after PA 233 of 2023; pending litigation against the MPSC over PA 233 implementation; infrastructure capacity. Active as of 2026-09-23; Ordinance No. 646 took effect on publication after 2026-07-27 adoption and runs until BESS regulations are adopted. Legal basis: Charter Township of Kalamazoo Ordinance No. 646, temporary moratorium on battery energy storage facilities.

NewEdge Renewable Power's proposed 260 MW BESS at West M Avenue and South Van Kal Street; PA 233 state siting. Active as of 2026-09-23; set to expire 2026-11-25. Board announced in July 2026 it plans to extend it; draft Energy Systems Ordinance under Planning Commission review since 2026-08-13. Legal basis: (first instrument, November 2025) Oshtemo Charter Township ordinance imposing a one-year moratorium on commercial energy storage system (BESS) development, adopted 5-2 on first reading and unanimously (two absent) on second/final reading at the November 25, 2025 Township Board meeting; specific ordinance number not confirmed despite checking the township's PA233-BESS information page, its Notices archive, news coverage (MLive, Energy-Storage.news), and the encodeplus.com compiled-ordinance viewer (which does show Ordinance No. 688, the later data-center moratorium, and No. 695, the later solar moratorium, but the relevant section for the November 2025 BESS moratorium could not be located by section ID).

Need for siting, design, construction and decommissioning standards for large-scale solar while Energy Systems Ordinance is drafted. Active as of 2026-09-23; six-month moratorium on new principal-use (large-scale) solar applications adopted 2026-08-11. Legal basis: Oshtemo Charter Township Ordinance No. 695, an ordinance imposing a moratorium on Solar Energy Development for Principal-Use SES, Principal-Use (Large) SES, and Principal-Use (Small) SES, adopted at the August 11, 2026 Township Board meeting (second reading; first reading July 28, 2026), published August 20, 2026.

Preemptive; no applications received; concern about BESS fire risk and data center water/energy impacts. Active as of 2026-09-23; runs to 2026-12-31. On 2026-09-22 the city development officer told council the moratorium may need to be extended because rezoning work must finish first. Legal basis: City of Portage Ordinances O-2-2026 (Chapter 42 Article 13, Secs. 42-1302/42-1303) and O-3-2026 (Sec. 42-140 zoning temporary moratorium).

Allow time to study and potentially adopt revised regulations governing data centers and BESS. Active as of 2026-09-23; one-year moratorium adopted 2026-04-21 runs to approximately 2027-04-21. Legal basis: Ordinance No. 26-02, Ordinance Establishing Data Center and Battery Energy Storage System Moratorium (Police Power).

Master plan update underway; Silver Maple Solar (RWE Americas, ~200 MW) dispute and township lawsuit challenging PA 233; desire to maintain status quo on energy facilities and data centers until zoning is updated. Active as of 2026-09-23; one-year moratorium on commercial energy facilities (solar, wind, battery storage) and data centers (definition includes crypto-mining facilities) adopted 2026-09-01, runs 365 days from publication of the notice of adoption (approximately early September 2027). Legal basis: Township Board resolution 'A Resolution Enacting Temporary Moratoria on Energy Facilities and Data Centers' adopted 2026-09-01 under Section 3.36 of the Zeeland Charter Township Zoning Ordinance (number blank in the board packet); it repealed and superseded the township's March 3, 2026 moratorium (No. 1027), which has its own row.
